test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 3 Feb 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is necessarily a final good?
solution:
The correct answer is __**An XL size shirt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Final product**:

 
 
• A **final good or consumer good** is a** final product ready for sale** that is **used by the consumer to satisfy current wants or needs**, unlike intermediate goods which are utilized to produce other goods. 
 
• **Cotton is a raw material** used to make shirts. So an XL size shirt is** necessarily** a final product.
 
• When used in measures of** national income and output**, the term "final goods" includes only new goods.
 
 
 
• The final product is of two types:
 
 
• **Personal consumption (like bread purchased by consumer household)**.
 
• **Investment or capital formation (like building, machinery purchased by a firm).**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Intermediate good**:

 
 
• Intermediate goods are referred to as those goods that are **used for producing final goods**.
 
• Intermediate goods are** not included in the national income** and therefore have no impact.
 
• A** particular brand of tea is an intermediate good **as it is still** not ready to consume**.
